"**Who was Iraj Khajeh Amiri?**"

"Iraj Khajeh Amiri (born Hossein Khajeh Amiri Khaledi, 1933–2026) was one of Iran’s most beloved and respected classical singers. He was widely known by his stage name, **Iraj**, and was affectionately nicknamed **"Pahlavan-e Avaz"** (Champion of Song)."

"Born into a musical family in Khaled Abad, near Kashan, he began studying traditional Persian singing (*avaz*) under his father at the age of six. Over a career spanning more than seven decades, he became a towering figure in Iranian classical music, often mentioned alongside legends like Mohammad-Reza Shajarian."

"Beyond his singing, Iraj was also a retired army officer and performed in many Iranian films before the 1979 Islamic Revolution. After the revolution, he stopped appearing in movies but continued his musical career and teaching, founding a music school in Tehran. His son, Ehsan Khajeh Amiri, is also a well-known Iranian pop singer."

"Iraj passed away on August 12, 2026, at the age of 94. His funeral ceremony, held at Tehran’s Vahdat Hall, drew a large crowd of ordinary citizens as well as artists, musicians, and cultural figures—a testament to his enduring legacy as one of the great voices of Persian traditional music.
